Name: Rome
Desc: The sprawling heart of the Empire, a vast metropolis that consumes the tribute of a continent and projects power across the known world.

Name: Athens
Desc: The cradle of Western philosophy and democracy, famed for its monumental Acropolis, fine pottery, and bustling port of Piraeus.

Name: Carthage
Desc: Rome's great rival, a mercantile powerhouse on the African coast, built on maritime trade and control of the seas before its fateful fall.

Name: Alexandria
Desc: The intellectual and commercial hub of the Mediterranean, home to the Great Library and the Lighthouse, where Eastern goods meet Western markets.

Name: Antioch
Desc: A luxurious and cosmopolitan city near the Levant coast, serving as a major western terminus of the Silk Road and a gateway to Persia.

Name: Tyre
PrimaryProducts: Tyrian Purple Dye;Cedar Timber;Blown Glass;Fine Linen
Desc: An ancient Phoenician island fortress, legendary for its resilient defenders, skilled sailors, and the priceless purple dye harvested from its shores.

Name: Babylon
Desc: The ancient, magnificent capital of Mesopotamia, famed for its ziggurats and hanging gardens, situated on the fertile banks of the Euphrates.

Name: Memphis
Desc: The ancient capital of Lower Egypt, a city of immense religious importance and the administrative center for the wealth of the Nile Delta.

Name: Istanbul
Desc: The city on two continents, holding the strategic key to the Bosphorus strait and controlling all trade between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.

Name: Cadiz
Desc: A vital Phoenician and later Roman port on the Atlantic, a gateway for the mineral wealth of Hispania and trade from the mysterious northern seas.

Name: Marseille
Desc: An old Greek colony on the coast of Gaul, serving as a key entry point for Roman goods and culture into the Celtic hinterlands.

Name: Corinth
Desc: A wealthy Greek city controlling the strategic isthmus between the Peloponnese and mainland Greece, famed for its high-quality pottery and bronze.

Name: Ephesus
Desc: A bustling metropolis in western Anatolia, home to the great Temple of Artemis and a major center for trade and pilgrimage.

Name: Palmyra
Desc: A wealthy caravan city rising from the Syrian desert, a vital and often independent link on the Silk Road between the Roman and Persian spheres.

Name: Petra
Desc: The hidden capital of the Nabataeans, carved from red desert rock, which grew rich by controlling the lucrative incense trade routes from Arabia.

Name: Leptis Magna
Desc: A splendid Roman port city on the Libyan coast, which flourished as a major exporter of olive oil and exotic animals for the gladiatorial games.

Name: Syracuse
Desc: The most powerful Greek city in Sicily, a major naval and commercial power that often challenged Athens and Carthage for dominance.

Name: Meroë
Desc: The capital of the Kingdom of Kush, a southern powerhouse known for its distinctive pyramids, iron production, and trade in exotic African goods.

Name: Lothal
Desc: One of the most prominent cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, featuring a massive and sophisticated dock for maritime trade.

Name: Ur
Desc: A mighty Sumerian city-state in southern Mesopotamia, a cradle of civilization and an early hub for trade with lands across the Persian Gulf.

Name: Xi'an
Desc: The grand eastern terminus of the Silk Road and capital of powerful Chinese dynasties, a center of immense wealth, culture, and innovation.

Name: London
Desc: A bustling Roman port and administrative center on the River Thames, the heart of commerce for the remote province of Britannia.

Name: Lyon
Desc: The capital of the Three Gauls and a major Roman administrative and industrial center, known for its mint and pottery production.

Name: Paris
Desc: A modest settlement of the Parisii tribe on an island in the Seine, which grew into a significant regional center under Roman rule.

Name: Trier
Desc: A major Roman city on the Moselle River, which eventually became an imperial capital and one of the largest cities in the empire.

Name: Cologne
Desc: A key Roman military outpost and provincial capital on the Rhine frontier, guarding the empire against Germanic tribes.

Name: Cordoba
Desc: A major Roman and later Umayyad capital in Hispania, famed for its high-quality olive oil, leatherwork, and intellectual pursuits.

Name: Tarragona
Desc: The oldest Roman settlement in Hispania, serving as a major port and the administrative capital of a vast province.

Name: Mérida
Desc: A grand city founded for veteran legionaries, known for its impressive Roman engineering, including theaters, bridges, and aqueducts.

Name: Ravenna
Desc: A strategic port city surrounded by marshes, which became the last capital of the Western Roman Empire and a bastion of Byzantine art.

Name: Aquileia
Desc: A major Roman city at the head of the Adriatic Sea, a crossroads for trade in amber, iron, and wine between Italy and the northern provinces.

Name: Sparta
Desc: A famously militaristic Greek city-state in the Peloponnese, valued more for its disciplined soldiers than for its material trade goods.

Name: Thebes
Desc: A powerful city in Boeotia and a frequent rival of Athens, known for its legendary Sacred Band and strength in cavalry.

Name: Pergamon
Desc: A great Hellenistic capital in Anatolia, home to a massive library and the legendary inventor of parchment as a substitute for papyrus.

Name: Miletus
Desc: An ancient Ionian Greek city, a birthplace of philosophy and science, and a major producer of fine woolen textiles.

Name: Halicarnassus
Desc: A coastal Carian city famed as the site of the Mausoleum, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

Name: Sardis
Desc: The wealthy capital of the ancient Kingdom of Lydia, where coinage was first invented, situated on a key crossroads of Anatolian trade.

Name: Tarsus
Desc: The capital of Roman Cilicia, a center of learning and the primary producer of cilicium, a durable cloth made from goat hair.

Name: Damascus
PrimaryProducts: Damascus Steel;Inlaid Wood Box;Dried Apricots;Blown Glass
Desc: One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, a vital oasis and trade hub connecting Mesopotamia with the Mediterranean coast.

Name: Jerusalem
Desc: A city of immense religious significance to multiple faiths, drawing pilgrims from across the world and exporting local holy goods.

Name: Sidon
PrimaryProducts: Blown Glass;Tyrian Purple Dye;Cedar Timber;Salted Fish
Desc: A great Phoenician port city, sister and rival to Tyre, renowned for its skilled glassblowers and maritime trade network.

Name: Byblos
Desc: An ancient port city so intertwined with the papyrus trade that the Greek word for book, 'biblos', derives from its name.

Name: Dura-Europos
Desc: A fortress city on the Euphrates, a multicultural crossroads between the Roman and Parthian empires, perfectly preserved by the desert sands.

Name: Nineveh
Desc: The magnificent capital of the formidable Assyrian Empire, one of the largest cities in the world at its height.

Name: Persepolis
Desc: The grand ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, built to inspire awe and receive the tribute of subject nations.

Name: Susa
Desc: A major administrative capital of the Persian and later empires, strategically located between the Mesopotamian lowlands and the Iranian plateau.

Name: Ctesiphon
Desc: The sprawling winter capital of the Parthian and Sasanian Empires, famed for its colossal vaulted arch, the largest single-span brick arch in the world.

Name: Hatra
Desc: A fortified desert city that grew wealthy as a religious and trade center, known for its unique blend of Greek, Roman, and Parthian art.

Name: Luxor
Desc: The great capital of New Kingdom Egypt, a vast religious complex centered on the monumental temples of Karnak and Luxor.

Name: Cyrene
Desc: A prosperous Greek colony in Libya, whose wealth was founded on the cultivation and trade of the now-extinct, highly valuable plant Silphium.

Name: Volubilis
Desc: An important Roman provincial city on the western frontier of Africa, a center for the region's agricultural wealth.

Name: Cherchell
Desc: The capital of the Roman province of Mauretania, a bustling port city with a distinct Greco-Roman character.

Name: Samarkand
Desc: A legendary oasis city on the Silk Road, a Sogdian center of trade connecting China, India, and Persia.

Name: Bukhara
Desc: Another major Silk Road city, renowned for its crafts, carpets, and as a center of learning and culture in Central Asia.

Name: Merv
Desc: A massive oasis city in the Karakum Desert, a vital stop on the Silk Road and one of the largest cities in the world at its peak.

Name: Taxila
Desc: A bustling crossroads of cultures and learning in ancient India, where Greek, Persian, and Indian influences converged around a great university.

Name: Pataliputra
Desc: The grand capital of the Mauryan Empire in India, a massive and sophisticated city on the banks of the Ganges.

Name: Muziris
Desc: A legendary port on the Malabar Coast of India, which vanished from history. It was the epicenter of the lucrative spice trade with the Roman Empire.

Name: Berenice
Desc: A key Ptolemaic and Roman port on the Red Sea, built to secure the trade route for war elephants and spices from the East.

Name: Hegra
Desc: The southern sister-city to Petra, a Nabataean caravan city known for its spectacular rock-cut tombs, controlling the Incense Route.

Name: Milan
Desc: A major city in northern Italy that grew in importance to become an administrative center and de facto capital of the late Western Roman Empire.

Name: Bordeaux
Desc: A flourishing port city in southwestern Gaul, the center of a major wine-producing region whose goods were shipped across the empire.

Name: York
Desc: A rugged legionary fortress and administrative capital on the northern frontier of Roman Britain, guarding against the untamed tribes beyond.

Name: Brindisi
Desc: The primary Roman port of embarkation for Greece and the East, marking the terminus of the great Via Appia.

Name: Tangier
Desc: The capital of the Roman province of Mauretania Tingitana and a key port controlling the Strait of Gibraltar.

Name: Seleucia
Desc: A great Hellenistic metropolis founded on the Tigris, which for centuries rivaled Babylon and Alexandria in size and commercial importance.

Name: Hamadan
Desc: The ancient capital of the Medes, located at a high altitude on a key leg of the Silk Road connecting Mesopotamia to Central Asia.

Name: Artaxata
Desc: The grand capital of ancient Armenia, strategically located on the Araxes River at a crossroads between the Roman, Parthian, and Caucasian worlds.

Name: Bharuch
Desc: A major trade port in Gujarat, India, known to Greco-Roman geographers as a vital center for the lucrative Indian Ocean trade.

Name: Plovdiv
Desc: A large, prosperous city in the Roman province of Thrace, strategically located on the major military road to the East.

Name: Solin
Desc: The bustling capital of the Roman province of Dalmatia, a major port on the Adriatic coast.

Name: Angkor
Desc: The vast capital of the Khmer Empire, a sprawling urban and religious complex sustained by a sophisticated irrigation system that produced immense agricultural wealth.

Name: Ayutthaya
Desc: A cosmopolitan island capital and trading powerhouse that served as a crucial intermediary for goods flowing between the Indian Ocean, South China Sea, and beyond.

Name: Malacca
Desc: A legendary and wealthy entrepôt controlling the strategic Strait of Malacca, it was the vital global center for the lucrative spice trade from the East Indies.

Name: Palembang
Desc: The likely capital of the Srivijayan maritime empire, which dominated sea lanes and grew rich by controlling and taxing the vast trade passing through its waters.

Name: Oc Eo
Desc: A key port city of the Funan Kingdom in the Mekong Delta, it was a surprisingly cosmopolitan hub with trade connections stretching as far as the Roman Empire.

Name: Bolghar
Desc: A major trade hub on the Volga river, connecting the Norse, Russians, and the Islamic world, known for its lucrative leather and fur trade.

Name: Karakorum
Desc: The legendary capital of the vast Mongol Empire, a cosmopolitan center of administration, trade, and religion on the windswept steppes.

Name: Beijing
Desc: The grand northern capital of Kublai Khan's Yuan Dynasty, a meticulously planned imperial city and a major center of power and culture.

Name: Nanjing
Desc: A major southern capital for numerous Chinese dynasties, famed for its massive city walls, rich culture, and production of high-quality silks and textiles.

Name: Guangzhou
Desc: China's most enduring maritime gateway, a bustling port city on the Pearl River that has connected the empire to global sea trade for millennia.

Name: Arkaim
Desc: A fortified Bronze Age settlement in the Ural steppes, considered a proto-city and a key site for understanding the origins of Indo-European cultures and chariot technology.

Name: Ukek
Desc: A significant city of the Golden Horde on the Volga, a multicultural center for crafts and trade before its destruction by Tamerlane.

Name: Mangazeya
Desc: A short-lived but vital 17th-century Russian trading colony in the Siberian arctic, built entirely around the fabulously wealthy fur trade.
